query: For the equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy and its equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets that are single-phase FCC after thermomechanical processing, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain why their mechanical properties differ during deformation and failure when constituent count alone is inadequate? Specify a controlled comparison, predictions relative to the quinary baseline, the applicable boundary conditions, supporting evidence, and a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The differences in deformation and failure behavior among single-phase FCC Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni quinary alloys and their quaternary/ternary subsets are primarily due to differences in local lattice distortion and short‐range chemical ordering that arise when one or more elements are removed. These changes modify the barriers to dislocation motion and alter slip mechanisms during deformation.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic, single-phase FCC Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni (quinary) alloy and its equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets produced by identical thermomechanical processing.
generation.intervention: Remove one or two elements from the quinary alloy to form the quaternary and ternary systems while keeping the processing history constant, ensuring that all samples maintain a single-phase FCC structure.
generation.conditions: Room temperature tensile testing (and complementary deformation tests) under identical strain rates and processing conditions.
generation.structural_mediator: Local lattice distortions and emergent short-range chemical order that influence dislocation mobility.
generation.mechanism: The full quinary alloy’s higher elemental complexity creates heterogeneous internal stress fields and enhanced short‐range ordering, which impede dislocation glide and promote higher strain hardening. In contrast, reduced constituent systems exhibit less lattice distortion and diminished short-range ordering, leading to lower yield strength and altered strain hardening behavior during deformation.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the quinary baseline, the quaternary and ternary alloys are predicted to have lower yield strength and modified strain-hardening profiles (potentially 10–20% lower yield strength), reflecting easier dislocation motion due to reduced lattice distortion and less pronounced short-range ordering.
generation.baseline: The equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni (quinary) alloy processed into a single-phase FCC microstructure under identical thermomechanical conditions.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis applies when all compared alloys are processed under identical thermomechanical conditions (ensuring comparable single-phase FCC structures) and tested at room temperature under similar deformation rates.
generation.uncertainty: The quantitative extent to which lattice distortion and short-range ordering affect dislocation mobility is uncertain without direct atomic-scale measurements. Further characterization is required to firmly link these features to the observed mechanical differences.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare equiatomic single-phase FCC samples of the Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni quinary alloy and its quaternary/ternary subsets using identical thermomechanical processing. Conduct room temperature tensile tests to measure yield strength, strain hardening, and ductility. Complement these tests with atomic-scale characterization (e.g., high resolution TEM, atom probe tomography, or XRD line broadening) to quantify local lattice distortions and evidence of short-range ordering.
measurements: Tensile mechanical properties (yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, elongation, strain hardening rate)
Dislocation structures and density via TEM
Quantitative indicators of lattice distortion and short-range order from atom probe tomography or XRD analysis
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the mechanical properties (e.g., yield strength and strain hardening behavior) of the quaternary and ternary alloys do not show systematic differences correlated with measurable differences in lattice distortion and short-range ordering relative to the quinary alloy, or if all systems exhibit statistically indistinguishable deformation responses despite variations in elemental complexity, then the hypothesis is falsified.

System: Equiatomic Co20Cr20Fe20Ni20Mn20 (atomic percentage) FCC-structured high-entropy alloy. Test conditions: Tensile creep tests at 500, 550, and 600 °C under applied stresses of 140–400 MPa; interrupted tests at steady-state stages cooled with liquid nitrogen.
